durabilityMechanism.freshRun: main refuses either existing stable output path before browser dependency loading or capture execution.
durabilityMechanism.withinRun: Every checkpoint first writes a SHA-256-named archive using exclusive creation. Existing identical archive bytes are accepted without a rewrite; conflicting bytes fail. Only after archive preservation does the temporary-file rename update the stable latest path.
durabilityMechanism.archiveConflict: Tool leaves conflicting archive bytes and existing stable output unchanged.
durabilityMechanism.latestWriteFailure: Existing stable output remains intact in the tested temporary-file collision and rename-failure paths; the new exact-byte archive remains available.
durabilityMechanism.wiring: The CLI fresh-run guard executes once; normal internal checkpoint updates use the versioned writer at priority/full-route/final-projection stages.
limits: Atomicity is per stable file. Snapshot and summary are not a two-file transaction; a failure between them can leave their latest paths at different revisions, while each completed archive remains available.
The fresh-path check is a normal single-writer run guard, not a cross-process lock. Use distinct output paths for concurrent runs.
Filesystem permissions, external file edits and hardware-level durability are outside the immutability claim; the tool itself refuses to replace existing archive bytes.
